stem: The hydrogen halides $\text{HCl}$, $\text{HBr}$ and $\text{HI}$ are all colourless gases at room temperature.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
The hydrogen halides can be formed by reacting the halogens with hydrogen.

Describe and explain the relative reactivity of the halogens down the group when they react with hydrogen to form $\text{HCl}$, $\text{HBr}$ and $\text{HI}$.

parts.label: (b)
(b)(ii)
parts.text:
In reaction 2, $\text{NaCl}$ reacts with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ to form $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{NaHSO}_4$. When $\text{NaBr}$ reacts with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$, the products include $\text{Br}_2$ and $\text{SO}_2$.

Identify the type(s) of reaction that occur in each case by completing Table 3.1.

Explain the difference in these reactions.

Table 3.1

| reactants | type(s) of reaction |
| :--- | :--- |
| $\text{NaCl}$ and concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ |  |
| $\text{NaBr}$ and concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ |  |

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
When heated with a Bunsen burner, $\text{HCl}$ does not decompose, whereas $\text{HI}$ forms $\text{H}_2$ and $\text{I}_2$.

Explain the difference in the effect of heating on $\text{HCl}$ and $\text{HI}$.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
The hydrogen halides dissolve in water to form strong Brønsted-Lowry acids.

The concentration of a strong acid can be determined by titration.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text: State what is meant by strong Brønsted-Lowry acid.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:

- $0.1\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{NaOH(aq)}$ is added to $25\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.1\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{HBr(aq)}$, to excess
- $0.1\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{NH}_3\text{(aq)}$ is added to $25\text{ cm}^3$ of $0.1\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{HBr(aq)}$, to excess.

parts.text: $\text{HBr}$ reacts with propene to form two bromoalkanes, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ and $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHBr}$.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.text:
Complete the diagram to show the mechanism of the reaction of $\text{HBr}$ and propene to form the major organic product. Include charges, dipoles, lone pairs of electrons and curly arrows, as appropriate. Draw the structures of the intermediate and the major organic product.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text: Explain why the two bromoalkanes are not produced in equal amounts by this reaction.
